description.text:
In the Old Forest, the hobbits meet Tom Bombadil—a mysterious and ancient being, seemingly as old as the woods themselves.

At the Council of Elrond, the idea of giving the Ring to Tom is discussed, since he is immune to its corruption. Yet he is also immune to its burden and responsibility. Tom cannot be entrusted with the Ring: he would not understand its importance, might forget it entirely, and would never think to guard it.
Amon Sûl, the ancient watchtower, stands lonely on the hilltop. Frodo was struck here by the Morgul blade, a wound that would trouble him for the rest of the journey.

The road crosses the River Mitheithel at the Last Bridge. Travelers following an older trail might pause here to consider their supplies, inspect the current, and decide whether to ford the river. Or, just use the bridge?
Do you hear a voice on the wind? The Fellowship first tried to cross the Pass of Caradhras. You will have to find another route too.

The Doors of Durin mark the secret entrance to the ancient Dwarven city of Moria. They guard a vast network of mines and halls, once filled with wealth and life but now abandoned to shadow and danger.
I hope you haven't eaten all your lembas bread yet. One small bite is enough to fill the stomach of a grown man.

The Pillars of Kings are massive statues of Isildur and Anárion carved from living rock.

They guard the northern approach to Gondor, standing as silent monuments to the realm’s ancient power.

A maze of jagged hills and twisting ravines. Frodo and Sam struggled to find their way through the terrain, and here they first captured Gollum, who would become both guide and nemesis on their journey.

A cursed wetland, the Dead Marshes are filled with the bodies of men who fell in the ancient Battle of the Dagorlad. Pale faces and ghostly lights hover above the water, a grim reminder of the cost of war and the lands it scarred.

The dark tunnel of Cirith Ungol is home to Shelob, the last child of Ungoliant, a primordial spider-like being.  She has dwelt here for ages, a massive and ancient creature lurking in the shadows, her lair a quiet, web-filled labyrinth.

The barren plains of Mordor stretch beneath a sky of ash and fire. Scorched earth, blackened rocks, and poisoned soil make this a desolate wasteland, the heart of Sauron’s realm and the final stretch on the road to Mount Doom.
